title: How advertisers make us spend money
speaker: BBC Learning English

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Pippa. And I'm Phil. What's the last thing you bought and why did you buy it?
sentences.zh: 我是皮帕,我是菲尔,你最后买的是什么?

sentences.en: I bought a new pair of headphones recently because my old ones broke, and I did lots of research to try and find a good pair.
sentences.zh: 我最近买了一双新耳机 因为我的旧耳机坏了, 我做了很多研究 试图找到一对好。

sentences.en: How about you? I bought a soft drink on the way to work this morning.
sentences.zh: 你怎么样 我今早上班的路上买了一杯软饮料

sentences.en: It might be because I saw someone I like promoting it in an advert.
sentences.zh: 可能是因为我看到一个我喜欢在广告里宣传的人

sentences.en: We call this a celebrity endorsement. But why do they work?
sentences.zh: 我们称这为名人背书,但为什么要工作?

sentences.en: Let's start by hearing from Ben Jones, a behavioural research expert, speaking to BBC World Service programme Business Daily.
sentences.zh: 我们先听听Ben Jones 的行为研究专家 在BBC世界服务节目《商业日报》上的发言

sentences.en: When we're unsure, we don't know what to do, it's kind of easy to follow the lead of those who we think are credible or knowledgeable.
sentences.zh: 当我们不确定,我们不知道该怎么办, 很容易跟随那些我们认为可信或知情的人。

sentences.en: It's a mental shortcut. It's something that helps us navigate uncertain times or make quick choices.
sentences.zh: 这是一个心理捷径。它帮助我们在不确定的时代 或快速地做出选择。

sentences.en: We start doing that from an early age. Our parents… for some people, it's about our teachers – you know, these people who help us learn and make sense of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们从小就开始这样做。我们的父母,对一些人来说, 是关于我们的老师,你知道, 那些帮助我们学习和理解世界的人。

sentences.en: And some businesses can draw on this through things like endorsements – you know, dentists recommending toothpaste, athletes endorsing sportswear.
sentences.zh: 有些企业可以通过背书来利用这一点——你知道,牙医推荐牙膏,运动员认可运动服。

sentences.en: Ben says that endorsements work as a mental shortcut.
sentences.zh: Ben说背书是心理上的捷径

sentences.en: This is something that helps us make a decision quickly.
sentences.zh: 这有助于我们迅速作出决定。

sentences.en: If we trust the endorsement, then we don't need to think about it that much.
sentences.zh: 如果我们相信背书,那么我们就不需要考虑那么多了。

sentences.en: In this episode, we're going to look at the way that people can be convinced to do things.
sentences.zh: 在这一集中,我们将会看到人们如何被说服去做事情。

sentences.en: And as usual, we'll learn some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样,我们会学习一些有用的新词和新词。

sentences.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary and a quiz on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 记住,你会在我们的网站上 找到所有的词汇和测验,bbc学习英语。 com。

sentences.en: OK. But first I have a question for you, Pippa.
sentences.zh: 好吧 但首先我要问你一个问题 皮帕

sentences.en: Today we're talking about behavioural science.
sentences.zh: 今天我们谈论的行为科学。

sentences.en: What's the name of the theory that says people respond to small prompts?
sentences.zh: 说人们响应小提示的理论叫什么?

sentences.en: Is it: a) push theory, b) pull theory, or c) nudge theory?
sentences.zh: 是:a) 推论,b) 拉论,或c) 推论?

sentences.en: Oh, I'm not sure. I'm going to say b) pull theory.
sentences.zh: 我不确定 我要说b) 拉理论

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好吧,我们到节目结束时会找出答案的

sentences.en: In recent years, many fast-food chains have installed touchscreen machines for people to order their food.
sentences.zh: 近年来,许多快餐连锁店安装了触摸屏机,供人们订购食品。

sentences.en: They've reported taking more money as a result.
sentences.zh: 他们已经报告 更多的钱因此。

sentences.en: Could behavioural science tell us why this happens?
sentences.zh: 行为科学能告诉我们为什么会发生这种事吗?

sentences.en: Here's product designer Dean Ward speaking to BBC World Service's Business Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是产品设计师Dean Ward 在英国广播公司世界服务日报上讲话

sentences.en: Firstly, the psychology of speaking to someone and feeling judged – we think is a key factor.
sentences.zh: 首先,与某人交谈和判断感觉的心理——我们认为这是一个关键因素。

sentences.en: So, would you like extra fries? Would you like to go large?
sentences.zh: 你想多吃点薯条吗?

sentences.en: Not all people, but I think there's definitely a large proportion of people who may feel judged in those instances and may say no.
sentences.zh: 并非所有的人, 但我认为肯定有很大一部分人 可能会觉得在那种情况下会受到审判, 并且会说不。

sentences.en: There's the fact that you've got more time to look.
sentences.zh: 事实是,你有更多的时间去寻找。

sentences.en: You can see the product, you can see what's in it, you can see all the products linked to it as well.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到产品,你可以看到里面是什么, 你可以看到所有与它相关的产品。

sentences.en: And also around upsell as well. Would you like to add this?
sentences.zh: 也到处奔波,你要不要加上这个?

sentences.en: Would you like to do that? Because you've got more time and you're not being judged, you're very much more inclined to actually say yes to these things.
sentences.zh: 你愿意这么做吗?因为你有更多的时间,你没有被审判, 你更愿意对这些东西说"是"。

sentences.en: And that's typically what we're seeing – an increased basket spend of typically 25–30%.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们所看到的—— 增加的篮子支出通常为25-30%。

sentences.en: If people feel judged, then it means that they worry what other people will think of them.
sentences.zh: 如果人们觉得自己是被判断的 那么他们就会担心别人会怎么想

sentences.en: If we have to ask a human for extra fries, we might worry what they think of us, but no one feels judged by a computer screen.
sentences.zh: 如果我们需要向人类索取额外的薯条, 我们可能会担心他们对我们的看法, 但是没有人感到被电脑屏幕所评判。

sentences.en: If you upsell something, then you get someone to spend more.
sentences.zh: 如果你卖东西,你得到 有人花更多。

sentences.en: For example, waiters often try to get people to buy larger portions, more drinks, or dessert.
sentences.zh: 例如,服务员常常试图让人们购买大部分、更多的饮料或甜点。

sentences.en: Dean says that upselling can increase people's basket spend.
sentences.zh: Dean说上市可以增加人们的篮子开支

sentences.en: A basket spend is the total amount that someone spends in one transaction, on everything that's in their basket.
sentences.zh: 篮子支出是某人在一个交易中 花在篮子里的每样东西上的总金额

sentences.en: Now, this is an example of a business using behavioural science to nudge people to do things.
sentences.zh: 现在,这是一个例子 企业使用行为科学 激励人们做事情。

sentences.en: But it's not just businesses that use behavioural science in this way.
sentences.zh: 但不只是企业 使用行为科学的方式。

sentences.en: In Tunisia, the United Nations World Food Programme wanted to encourage people to eat food together more often.
sentences.zh: 在突尼斯,联合国世界粮食计划署希望鼓励人们更经常地一起吃饭。

sentences.en: They made a TV show set in a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 他们在一家餐馆里做了个电视剧

sentences.en: Let's hear from Takwa Khelifi from the World Food Programme, talking to BBC World Service's Business Daily.
sentences.zh: 让我们从世界粮食计划署的Takwa Khelifi那里听到BBC世界服务日报。

sentences.en: So, we needed something really creative and really different to think outside of the box, or to let people see themselves in those stories, because people are learning and changing by imitating and modelling and, like, observing others' behaviours and others' actions and emotional reactions to things.
sentences.zh: 所以,我们需要一些真正有创意和真正不同的东西 来从盒子外思考, 或者让人们看到自己在这些故事中, 因为人们正在学习和改变 通过模仿和建模, 像观察他人的行为 和其他人的行为 和情感反应。

sentences.en: So, this is why we tried this project or this... tried this product or this TV series – in order that you impact people.
sentences.zh: 所以,这就是为什么我们尝试这个项目或这个... 尝试这个产品或这个电视系列-- 以便你影响人们。

sentences.en: Takwa says that they needed to think outside the box.
sentences.zh: 塔克瓦说,他们需要思考 外面的盒子。

sentences.en: This means to try and think in a different way, to come up with something creative.
sentences.zh: 这意味着尝试以不同的方式思考, 提出一些创造性的东西。

sentences.en: The TV programme leads to people modelling behaviour.
sentences.zh: 电视节目导致人们模拟行为。

sentences.en: If you model behaviour, then you behave in a way that other people can copy.
sentences.zh: 如果你模拟行为, 那么你的行为方式 别人可以复制。

sentences.en: Now Phil, I think it's time to hear the answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 现在,菲尔,我想是时候 听到答案 你的问题。

sentences.en: Yes, it is. I asked what theory says that people respond to small prompts to change their behaviour.
sentences.zh: 是的,是的,我问理论是怎么说的 人们对小的冲动反应 来改变他们的行为。

sentences.en: I thought it was pull theory... ...which I'm afraid was the wrong answer.
sentences.zh: 我以为这是拉理论... 恐怕是错误的答案

sentences.en: Nudge theory says that people's behaviour can be changed by small prompts or nudges.
sentences.zh: Nudge理论说,人们的行为可以被小的推理或推理改变。

sentences.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with mental shortcut, which is something that helps us make a decision quickly, usually because we don't need to think about it.
sentences.zh: 好吧,让我们回顾一下我们学到的词汇, 从精神捷径开始, 这有助于我们快速做出决定, 通常因为我们不需要考虑它。

sentences.en: If someone feels judged, then they're worried about what other people think about them.
sentences.zh: 如果有人觉得被评判了 他们担心别人会怎么看待他们

sentences.en: Upsell refers to persuading someone to buy something extra, like a dessert at a restaurant.
sentences.zh: Upsell指的是说服别人买一些额外的东西 比如餐馆的甜点

sentences.en: Basket spend is what you spend in one transaction on the things in your shopping basket.
sentences.zh: 篮子是你们在一个交易中 花在购物篮里的东西上的钱

sentences.en: If you think outside the box, then you think about something in a different way to come up with a creative solution.
sentences.zh: 如果你在盒子外思考,那么你就会用不同的方式想出一个创新的解决方案。

sentences.en: And finally, modelling is behaving in a way that others can copy.
sentences.zh: 最后,模型的行为方式 使其他人可以复制。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but why not head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to try the quiz and worksheet for this episode.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了, 但为什么不直接去我们的网站,bbc学习英语.com, 来尝试这个片段的测验和工作表。

sentences.en: See you again soon! Bye!
sentences.zh: 回头见 再见
